requirement.text: Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, mediator-PA interaction protocols are defined.

classification.rationale: The requirement specifies defining interaction protocols between mediators and peering components (SR, PR, PA) in a Content Delivery Network (CDN) peering architecture. This relates to backend service communication and infrastructure protocols rather than a web application, mobile application, or machine learning system.

rounds.text_checked: Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, mediator-PA interaction protocols are defined.

issues.explanation: The requirement combines three separate interaction protocols (Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, and mediator-PA) into a single statement. These protocols represent distinct behaviors that can be specified, implemented, and tested independently.
Stating that protocols 'are defined' lacks specific functional requirements, operational capabilities, or testable pass/fail criteria to verify compliance.

questions.question_text: The phrase 'Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, mediator-PA interaction protocols' combines three distinct interaction protocols into a single requirement. Should this requirement be split into three separate requirements—one for each protocol (Mediator-SR, Mediator-PR, and Mediator-PA)?

The phrase 'are defined' lacks verifiable criteria. What specific functional behaviors, operational capabilities, or message exchange standards must these interaction protocols satisfy to allow compliance verification?

answers.answer_text: Keep this as one requirement. The bundled actions describe a single causal step (one trigger producing one behavior), not two independently testable behaviors -- splitting would fragment one atomic step rather than separate genuinely distinct requirements.

No pass/fail criterion exists for this in the source document; without a measurable acceptance threshold this cannot be made verifiable by answering a clarifying question -- it needs a threshold added by whoever owns the requirement, not invented here.

rounds.text_checked: Mediator-SR, mediator-PR, mediator-PA interaction protocols are defined.

test_strategy.rationale: Interaction protocols inherently involve sequences of states and message exchanges between the Mediator and other entities (SR, PR, PA), driving state transitions. Additionally, protocol interactions define multi-step scenarios between components and serve as a dependency for operational flows like PURE-PEERING-0013, making 'use_case' testing highly appropriate.

test_cases.title: Mediator-SR Protocol State Transition Validation
test_cases.preconditions: Mediator and Service Requestor/Registry (SR) components are initialized and in Idle state.
steps: Initiate session connection message from Mediator to SR.
Verify Mediator-SR connection state transitions from Idle to Connecting.
Send protocol capability handshake request message and receive valid response.
Verify Mediator-SR connection state transitions from Connecting to Connected.
Send session teardown request message and verify state transitions from Connected to Terminated.
test_cases.expected_result: Mediator-SR state transitions strictly follow the defined protocol lifecycle without entering illegal states.

test_cases.title: Mediator-PR Protocol State Transition and Exception Handling
test_cases.preconditions: Mediator and Peering Router/Provider (PR) communication channels are active.
steps: Send protocol initialization message from Mediator to PR.
Verify state transitions from Uninitialized to Negotiating.
Inject invalid message sequence header according to protocol specification.
Verify state transitions from Negotiating to Error handling state.
Send reset protocol control message and confirm transition back to Uninitialized state.
test_cases.expected_result: Mediator-PR state machine accurately updates connection states and handles protocol exceptions as defined.

test_cases.title: Mediator-PA Interaction Protocol Sequence for Negotiation Establishment
test_cases.preconditions: Peering Agent (PA) and Mediator endpoints are online and configured to initiate peering negotiation.
steps: PA initiates negotiation sequence by sending a protocol request to the Mediator.
Mediator processes request and returns protocol handshake response containing valid negotiation parameters.
PA acknowledges negotiation parameters via Mediator-PA response protocol packet.
Mediator finalizes session creation and registers active PA negotiation context.
test_cases.expected_result: Mediator-PA interaction protocol sequence completes successfully, enabling PA operational negotiation flow.
